title: Knowledge check: Code Quality and Maintainability

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Code Quality and Maintainability”?
options: A project is maintainable when it has no setup documentation.
A safe migration begins with dependency/behavior inventory, tests, small reversible changes, and documentation.
Change every package at once without a rollback plan.
Legacy Vue 2 projects receive all current Vue 3 features automatically.
questions.answer_key: A safe migration begins with dependency/behavior inventory, tests, small reversible changes, and documentation.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Code Quality and Maintainability directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Consistent naming conventions”, which practice is most reliable?
options: A safe migration begins with dependency/behavior inventory, tests, small reversible changes, and documentation.
Change every package at once without a rollback plan.
Legacy Vue 2 projects receive all current Vue 3 features automatically.
A project is maintainable when it has no setup documentation.
questions.answer_key: A safe migration begins with dependency/behavior inventory, tests, small reversible changes, and documentation.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Consistent naming conventions”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Code Quality and Maintainability” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
